name: West Face

pitch_detail.notes: Right-facing dihedral high on the route.
Finish up the face and left to the summit.

rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 1 of 2, about 35 m north, to the notch. A 35 m rappel needs two ropes or a 70 m rope.
rappel_detail.anchor: summit anchor (build or back up with cord)
hazards: Do not plan on reversing the loose line of ascent.
rappel_detail.station: The summit, shared by every route on the peak.

rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 2 of 2, east onto the Blue Glacier.
rappel_detail.anchor: anchor at the notch (build or back up with cord)
hazards: The last rappel can hang free over the moat at the foot of the face. Land beyond the lip.
rappel_detail.station: The notch north of the summit.

rappels: 2 rappels off the shared summit: about 35 m north to the notch, then east onto the Blue Glacier
approach: The genuine standard approach is from the Downey Creek Trailhead (off Suiattle River Road) via the southern end of the Ptarmigan Traverse — a rugged, largely off-trail alpine route over Itswoot Ridge/Cub Lake and Bachelor Creek involving glacier travel and significant bushwhacking. Climbers typically budget a full day (or two) of approach before reaching the base of South Peak's granite faces; this is an experienced-mountaineers-only objective, not a roadside crag.
overview: The only route on this face.
fa: Cliff Leight and a partner, early 1990s
